newsitem.title: USA: KCBT president sees spread opportunity in CBOT Dow.
newsitem.headline: KCBT president sees spread opportunity in CBOT Dow.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade's license to list products based on the bellwether Dow Jones Industrial Average is good news for the Kansas City Board of Trade, KCBT president Michael Braude said Thursday.
In an interview, Braude said the CBOT's proposed Dow futures provide a "significant" new spread opportunity for the KCBT's Value Line stock index futures.
The two exchanges already have an active wheat futures spread, and Braude said he hoped their stock index products could follow suit.
"We certainly look at the Dow thing as a positive, not a negative," Braude said. "If the Dow (product) does well, then the Dow/Value Line spread is an excellent strategy."
A CBOT official said Thursday he "would not anticipate any problem with it at all."
The two exchanges already have a cross-margining agreement for their wheat futures contracts, which simplifies accounting of spreads between the two exchanges.
Dow Jones & Co granted licenses early last month to the CBOT, the American Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange to trade products based on the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
The CBOT plans to list futures and futures-options on the Dow before the end of the year, officials have said.
On the same day Dow Jones licensed its industrial index to the CBOT, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange announced it would launch a "mini" Standard and Poor's 500 futures index.
Braude cited spread potential with the proposed CME contract as well.
"A Mini Value Line/Mini S&P spread would be a great thing too," he said.
He noted that the CME and KCBT do not have a cross-margining agreement, but he said he had been in contact with CME president Rick Kilcollin about forging one.
